title: Benoni Defense: Classical Variation
line: White develops calmly, and Black's rook and knight aim at White's center pawn.

steps.text: The Benoni, as in the ideas lesson.
This time White brings the knight out instead of pushing another pawn forward.
Put the bishop on the long diagonal. Once your knight moves, it aims at White's queen's side.
Castle, to get your king to safety.
Put the rook on the open file. With the knight, it attacks the pawn on e4.
steps.after: White's knight steps back to guard the pawn.

steps.text: If White plays this instead, pushing the pawn on a2 to hold back your pawn on b7, the pawn on e4 is left with one guard.
Take the pawn with the knight.

steps.after: Black is a pawn up, and the rook stands in the center.

summary: The rook on the open file and the knight aim at the pawn in the center. Guard it badly and it falls.
